title: Sunny and the Blue Tongue Lizard | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka finds a blue-tongue lizard sunning itself on a warm flat rock in the moonlight, still and heavy-lidded and completely untroubled by the whole world. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The lizard was on the flat rock.

Sunny saw it from several steps away and slowed. A blue-tongue lizard — big and smooth and heavy-looking, stretched out in full across the warm surface of the rock. Its scales caught the moonlight in a way that made it look almost like polished wood. Its eyes were half-closed.

She approached very slowly.

The lizard watched her from its half-closed eyes. It did not move. It blinked, once, slowly — a long slow blink that seemed to say: I see you, and I have decided you are not very interesting.

Sunny sat down a respectful distance away.

The lizard continued to do nothing.

It was very good at doing nothing. Its legs were flat against the rock, its tail stretched behind it. Its belly pressed into the warm stone. The whole of its body said: I am perfectly comfortable exactly where I am.

She watched it breathe. In and out. Slow and deep, its whole sides expanding.

The tongue came out — blue and wide and flat, tasting the air — then back in.

She had never seen blue quite like that. A blue so bright it seemed lit from inside.

The lizard went back to its stillness.

She thought: to be that at home in your own skin must be a wonderful thing.

She lay down on the cool grass beside the rock.

The lizard dozed. Sunny dozed.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, blue tongue. Goodnight, little one.
